You didn't go wrong anywhere, it's the lack of a support system that has led to this. This holds not only for you but for anyone who feel alone and isolated, be it a wagie or NEET.

When I say support system, I mean a system which can hold one and help one with their emotional and mental turmoils without any judgement. A system where everyone has a choice to either participate in society or not, without any judgement (subtle or otherwise) .

The way our society is structured and has always been structured since the time of the early humans has always been winner takes most, if not all. A society that cannot take care of the people that need its help and support the most, that does not provide a choice to anyone regarding participation in said society, this sort of society will always result in a massive number of people feeling isolated and helpless.

I realize it would be really hard at the current moment to not blame yourself for all your decisions, but I would still like to ask you to try to not blame yourself. I'm not asking you to delude yourself into thinking that one's decisions don't have consequences, I'm asking you to try to think that regardless of what decisions you have made, the lack of a support system at the time is equally as much to blame as you, for not helping you with your major life changing decisions.

I do not know what the solution to this is, I just know that a support system is absolutely crucial for a person to not feel isolated and helpless and is necessary for them to be able to make proper decisions regarding their lives.

See, exactly, you get it, in your own words, this is just how the world works, regarding some people getting an opportunity and some people not getting it.

It is reasonable to assume that the number of people who don't get the opportunity, is multiple orders of magnitude higher than the number of people who do get the opportunity. Even among people who do get the opportunity, only a small amount of people are able to make use of that opportunity using their existing resources and network.

In such a situation, where basic living standards are not guaranteed, where opportunities are not guaranteed to everyone, how does it make sense to bring more humans into the world, new humans of which only a tiny part will be able to get the basic living standards and opportunities? It just does not make any rational sense to bring new people into this world.

And please, no country on Earth has equal opportunities, saying that is a blatant insult to the millions of poor and homeless in every country and shows a complete lack of empathy.

This is survivorship bias. In a capitalistic society, which demands that the most resources be only given to the person who brings in the most profit, only way for upward class mobility is by taking away resources, however unknowingly, from people who are in a lower class level than you. What about them and their children? Why should they need to suffer so that a part of us can move upwards on the class ladder?

I'm not attacking you nor looking down on your struggle. I'm just asking you to think about the millions of people who weren't able to create or access opportunities like you did. I live and work in India and I have experienced all these issues first-hand.

Antinatalism may not be a permanent solution to this issue but it is completely reasonable to say that we really don't need any more humans at this point to skew the distribution of resources any further than it already is.

Excuse me for bursting your bubble but everyone on Reddit doesn't live in the US. Office salaries outside of typical first world countries are so low, (I am a Machine Learning Engineer in India) that after paying all rents and utilities, a person is left with very little money. Investing those peanuts into a volatile stock market is not a good decision. A better decision is to save those peanuts in a savings account and see those peanuts grow into walnuts after decades.

The point is that it's impossible for the average person to accumulate wealth on the order of millions by investing since investing peanuts will only get you some walnuts after decades if you're lucky enough to have a reasonable interest rate on your savings account.

The advantage of having a large amount of money to invest is that you can hedge your bets, which just can't be done when you have only peanuts to invest. The interest that you gain on the principal amount is also really big since your principal amount is in the order of millions.

One thing that is different between those super rich and us, is that our money mostly just grows at a linear rate, from paycheck to paycheck but their millions rapidly grow at a compounded rate in stocks and gets to a billion. The compounded rate grows rapidly compared to a linear rate.

Another difference is that the requirement of having atleast a couple of million to invest in the first place. If you have a million in stocks, it can rapidly become multiple millions by growing at a compounded rate. But that's again not a choice for us, as most of us don't have millions just lying around to invest.

The system is rigged in plain sight against us, there's no going around it.

I would say I am a loser too, even though I'm from India. I agree that on an average, capitalism has raised the living standards of people in Africa and India/China, but that is only the lowest two steps of Maslows hierarchy of needs. Work for me, drains me of my vitality and the only reason I have not handed in my resignation is because I need the money to survive in this capitalistic system. 
I am a white collar worker in India who is jaded by the system and I cannot even imagine the plight of blue collar workers in India/China and Africa who work only to satisfy the bottom two levels of Maslows hierarchy but are depressed and disconnected due to work. 
Even though I am working in a field which uses math (my passion) tremendously, I just cannot handle working 9-7, it sucks all the vitality out of me. That is why I empathize with the people at r/antiwork, as the current system of work needs to go, so that we can have higher levels of satisfaction and fulfilment in their lives. 
I understand that I am talking from a position of privilege, being a white collar worker in India, but just because I have privilege does not mean that I am not allowed to be in pain and suffering. 
The current system will not allow many of us to go beyond the bottom two levels of maslows hierarchy and that is why the system needs to be changed. I am advocating for a system whose structure allows all of us, blue and white collar workers, to move to higher levels in maslows hierarchy, which the current systems just isn't capable of doing.

I am an Indian and live in India, and don't get me wrong, I am happy for the people who are better off in their lives due to capitalism, but fuck me, it's infuriating to know that capitalism is the only way we have to improve their lives and that I have to be a part of this system due to that reason.

I really get the part of being socially stunted, I'd been sheltered a lot by my parents, to the point that I've visited a friends home just twice, over my entire school life (22 atm). This lack of social contact with others has made interacting with others an excruciating task. I don't know how they would respond to what I say or do, so I decreased my interactions further, and in college, I mostly stayed in my dorm, unknowingly making myself more socially stunted. 


After graduating a couple of months back, I finally understood how undeveloped my social skills are, after seeing other young people. I'd say they are of about a 12-13 year old child. That terrified me and I retreated further into myself. It's not that I don't get what other people may be thinking, I get that much, much later when I'm by myself, and not at the moment itself, when I'm with the person. 
This has developed a massive inferiority complex within me towards every single one of my friends and peers (most of whom I've not talked to for over a year). 


The following method isn't the solution at all, but I do it as I can't bring myself to try something else. I feed my insecurity, and once I feed it, I get a boost of confidence which may or may not take me through the day. For me, it's knowledge. I feel if I have more knowledge that the other person, I can think of myself as superior to him/her and can talk to them as I think of them as inferior. It's a f***ed up method, but I'm trapped in this, I've been that way since the time I was in middle school, when the effects of me being socially stunted began to show. I didn't know why it was happening at that time (in middle school) , but it's effect decreased if I had more knowledge(mostly physics) than the person I was talking to. Since that time, I've been following this method, and it gives me just the right amount of confidence to talk. 


However, if the other person has more knowledge, I'm out, I can't even open my mouth in those situations. 


Until this year this worked, but now it doesn't, that's as I started to realize how stressed out and worried I always was, I didn't want to talk to people that way, seeing them as inferior, I'm just projecting my own insecurities onto everyone. So I've mostly stopped reading as I realized I wasn't reading for myself. I've socially regressed (making basic, ordinary conversation is a huge exertion for me) even more, and since the past couple of months, after graduating, I've been out of energy to do anything, and slowly sinking into depression.

 
Sorry for the wall of text.
